spec.formula: y = clamp(asr(acc, shift) + output_zero_point, output_min, output_max), acc = bias + a*a_multiplier + b*b_multiplier (int32, a and b int8)
spec.domain: from xnn_init_qs8_add_minmax_scalar_params: shift in [13, 30] (scale ratios in [2^-10, 2^8)); |a_multiplier|, |b_multiplier| <= 2^21 and the larger one >= 2^20 (either may be negative if a scale is negative); bias = 2^(shift-1) - a_multiplier*a_zero_point - b_multiplier*b_zero_point; output_min = -128 and output_max = 127 always (the init sets them); zero points in [-128, 127]
width_bounds: acc = 2^(shift-1) + am*(a - azp) + bm*(b - bzp): |a - azp| <= 255, so |acc| < 2^29 + 2*255*2^21 < 2^31 (no int32 overflow; the exact value always fits)
a*am alone needs 29 bits: a 32-bit chain is needed unless the multipliers are reduced first

exact reduction: if 2^k divides both am and bm (k <= shift), floor((bias + am*a + bm*b) / 2^shift) = floor((bias >> k) + (am>>k)*a + (bm>>k)*b) >> (shift - k)) (floor of a sum of integers plus a fraction in [0,1))
XNNPACK's bench quantization (all scale 1, zero point 0) and any residual add with one quantization give am = bm = 2^20 = 2^shift: then y = sat8(a + b - azp - bzp + ozp) exactly

asr then +ozp then clamp to [-128,127] equals: narrowing with saturation to int16 (vnclip, round-down) then saturating +ozp then saturating narrow to int8, because int16 saturation keeps every value outside [-383, 382] outside the int8 range

regimes.residual: one quantization for a, b and y: am = bm = 2^20
regimes.same-ab: am = bm, not a power of two
regimes.shift13: shift 13 (minimum), zero points at the extremes

measured.upstream: rvv_u1v / rvv_u2v: sign-extend to e32 at m4/m8, two vmul.vx, two vadd, vsra, vadd, vmax, vmin, two vncvt per element group (about 10 e32 ops)
measured.x280_costs: ALU ops cost 2 cycles per LMUL (an e32m8 op is 16 cycles); narrowing 4 per LMUL; vsetvl about 1; libgcc calls (e.g. __ctzdi2 for __builtin_ctz: XNNPACK compiles RVV without Zbb) cost far more than they save on small batches

candidates.application: replace vsra + vadd(ozp) + vmax + vmin at e32 and the two vncvt with vnclip.wx (e32->e16, vxrm round-down, saturating), vsadd ozp at e16, vnclip.wi 0 (e16->e8): exact by the saturation bound in the spec
candidates.expected_gain: removes 4 e32m8 ops (64 cycles per 128 elements) of the ~10
preconditions: output_min/output_max are -128/127 for every params the init produces
vxrm must be set to round-down (rdn) explicitly

candidates.application: acc = bias + a*am then vmacc.vx with b and bm: one op instead of vmul + vadd
start the accumulator from the bias with vmv.v.x / vmadd so no separate add is needed

dispatch once per call on proven predicates of (am, bm, shift, bias): e.g. am == bm == 2^shift (bench, residual adds) to an e16 path, shared-multiplier and power-of-two-factor paths, the general e32 path otherwise
candidates.expected_gain: 4-8x in the regimes with exact narrow paths (bench, residual); none elsewhere
preconditions: each path exact on its whole predicate domain; never test particular values seen in the matrix
predicates cost a few scalar ops (no libgcc calls)

candidates.title: Divide out the common power of two of both multipliers
candidates.application: k = min(ctz(am), ctz(bm), shift): use am>>k, bm>>k, bias>>k (arithmetic) and shift-k; when the reduced multipliers and bias keep acc within 16 bits for every int8 a, b (check the bound once per call), run the whole chain at e16 with widening ops from e8
candidates.expected_gain: e16 chains are half the cost of e32 at equal elements; e8->e16 widening replaces vsext.vf4
preconditions: prove the floor identity in the spec for the reduced terms
ctz without libgcc: a bounded loop or bit tricks, the X280 has Zbb but XNNPACK's -march does not

candidates.title: One multiply when am == bm
candidates.application: acc = bias + am*(a + b) with a + b computed at e16 (fits 9 bits): one widening/e32 multiply instead of two
candidates.expected_gain: one e32 multiply fewer in residual-style adds
preconditions: exact: integer distributivity, no overflow by the spec's bound

candidates.application: keep as much of the chain as possible at e16 (input sums, zero-point handling) and widen only for the multiply
vwadd/vwmul/vwmacc from e8/e16 instead of vsext.vf4 then e32 ops
candidates.expected_gain: skips the sign-extension ops (vsext.vf4 at e32m8 is 16+ cycles)
preconditions: scalar operand of .vx widening ops is SEW-wide: a 21-bit multiplier does not fit an e16 scalar

candidates.application: choose the LMUL that keeps e32 groups in registers without spills (e8m2 -> e32m8 as upstream, or e8m1 -> e32m4 with more ILP)
no __builtin_ctz/__builtin_clz in dispatch code (they become libgcc calls without Zbb)
candidates.expected_gain: avoids pf2's 0.82x at small batches in qs8-vcvt

candidates.application: compute derived scalars (reduced multipliers, shifts, folded bias) once before the loop
candidates.expected_gain: small batches (256) are dominated by setup

candidates.application: issue next iteration's loads of a and b before this iteration's chain
candidates.expected_gain: rejected on qs8-vcvt in L1 (0.97x); may matter with two input streams at DRAM sizes
